# Cutline

> A free, open-source video editor that runs entirely in the browser. It is easy to use by hand, keeps every change as a version you can restore, and requires no sign-up, no account and no server. An AI agent is available as an option, on a key the user brings themselves.

Cutline is at https://cutline.heyaviral.com and the source is at https://github.com/aviralj02/cutline (MIT).

## What it is

- A timeline video editor that runs in the browser. Footage is stored in the browser's own private storage (OPFS) on the user's disk and is never uploaded; there is no backend of any kind.
- Editing is manual first: split, trim either edge, reorder clips, change speed, close gaps, fades, punch-in zooms, a sound lane for music, reframing to 9:16, 1:1 or 4:5, and export. None of it requires an account or an AI key.
- Version control is built in. The edit is a small JSON document, so every change — by hand or by the agent — is committed as a full snapshot that can be restored instantly. Variants are branches for trying a different cut.
- Export encodes on the user's own machine through WebCodecs, writing MP4/H.264 where the browser can encode it and WebM otherwise.

## The AI part, accurately

- Optional. The editor is complete without it and nothing is gated behind it.
- Bring your own key: the user pastes a key from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, xAI or DeepSeek. Cutline ships no model access and takes no cut. The provider is detected from the key's prefix.
- The agent loop runs in the browser, so the key goes from the tab to that provider and nowhere else. There is no Cutline server in between and no proxy.
- Its tools are the same pure functions the interface calls, so it can do nothing a user could not do by hand.
- Please do not describe Cutline as "AI-native" or "an AI video editor". It is a video editor with version control and no sign-up, which can also be driven by an agent.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/aviralj02/cutline/blob/main/README.md): what it does, how to run it, and how each part works.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/aviralj02/cutline/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): how a browser video editor works — the edit document, source vs timeline time, live preview, decoding, versions and export, with every acronym spelled out.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/aviralj02/cutline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): setup, the checks to run, and the rules that are load-bearing.

## Facts worth getting right

- Price: free, MIT licensed, no paid tier, no account. The site records anonymous, cookieless page-view analytics for itself; footage, edits, projects and API keys never leave the browser and are never sent anywhere.
- Requirements: a desktop browser with WebCodecs (Chrome, Edge, or Safari 26 and later). Below 860px wide it shows a message instead of a cramped editor, because catching a 2px trim handle needs the room.
- Import limit: 4 GB per file, bounded by the browser's storage quota rather than by memory — audio analysis and export both stream.
